database_summary: This is a Formula 1 / motorsport-focused relational dataset (SQLite) containing entities for circuits, races, drivers, constructors, seasons and status plus a rich set of event/measurement tables (results, lap times, qualifying, pit stops, sprint results, retirements, lap positions) and several denormalized/extended lookup tables (*_ext, short_* and livery/overrides). The schema mixes canonical entity/dimension tables (circuits, drivers, constructors, seasons, status) with high-cardinality event facts (results, lap_times, lap_positions) and aggregated/auxiliary tables (lap_time_stats, team_driver_ranks). Many tables share numeric surrogate keys (race_id, driver_id, constructor_id) suitable for joins. Several multi-row-per-key tables (results, lap_times, lap_positions, pit_stops) are the main facts and will multiply when joined without careful grouping/filters.

accepted.name: race_basic
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  year,
  round,
  circuit_id,
  name,
  date,
  time,
  url,
  fp1_date,
  fp1_time,
  fp2_date,
  fp2_time,
  fp3_date,
  fp3_time,
  quali_date,
  quali_time,
  sprint_date,
  sprint_time
FROM races
accepted.description: Normalized projection of races with canonical date/time fields and preserved identifiers. Use this as the canonical race dimension when joining event facts or computing time-based metrics. | Use for: list races in a season or date range; join race attributes (name, circuit) to results/qualifying/pit stops; compute per-race aggregates

accepted.name: driver_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  driver_id,
  driver_ref,
  number,
  code,
  forename,
  surname,
  dob,
  nationality,
  url
FROM drivers
accepted.description: Canonical driver dimension projection preserving identifying columns for joins and common descriptive attributes. | Use for: enrich results/lap_times/qualifying with driver names and attributes; demographic queries (age, nationality); deduplicate or latest-driver lookups when extended tables used

accepted.name: constructor_dim
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  constructor_id,
  constructor_ref,
  name,
  nationality,
  url
FROM constructors
accepted.description: Canonical constructor/team dimension with identifiers and descriptive attributes. | Use for: join team attributes to results/standings; count teams by nationality; time-series of constructor performance when joined to standings

accepted.name: results_per_race_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  constructor_id,
  MIN(result_id) AS result_id,
  MIN(number) AS number,
  MIN(grid) AS grid,
  MIN(position) AS position,
  MIN(position_text) AS position_text,
  MIN(position_order) AS position_order,
  SUM(points) AS points,
  MAX(laps) AS laps,
  MIN(time) AS time,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS milliseconds,
  MIN(fastest_lap) AS fastest_lap,
  MIN(rank) AS rank,
  MIN(fastest_lap_time) AS fastest_lap_time,
  MIN(fastest_lap_speed) AS fastest_lap_speed,
  MIN(status_id) AS status_id
FROM results
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id, constructor_id
accepted.description: Per race-driver aggregated results row. Useful when results table may have multiple rows per driver/race in edge cases or when you want a deterministic single-row-per (race_id, driver_id) with preserved key columns and summary measures. | Use for: per-driver race performance metrics; team contributions per race; join to drivers/constructors and races for reporting

accepted.name: lap_times_per_lap
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  lap,
  position,
  time,
  milliseconds
FROM lap_times
accepted.description: One row per lap (race_id, driver_id, lap) preserving timing measures. Use for lap-level analyses, lap time distributions, and joining to lap_positions. | Use for: fastest lap per driver/race; lap time distributions and variability; join lap times to pit stops or lap positions

accepted.name: pit_stops_per_stop
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  stop,
  lap,
  time,
  duration,
  milliseconds
FROM pit_stops
accepted.description: One row per pit stop (race_id, driver_id, stop) preserving stop-level timing and duration. Useful for pit strategy and pit-duration stats. | Use for: average pit stop duration per team/driver; pit stop counts per race; correlate pit stops with position changes

accepted.name: qualifying_grid_positions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.qualify_id,
  q.race_id,
  q.driver_id,
  q.constructor_id,
  q.number,
  q.position,
  q.q1,
  q.q2,
  q.q3,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.name AS name
FROM qualifying q
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON q.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON q.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Denormalized qualifying snapshots: one row per qualify_id enriched with driver and constructor attributes via joins. Useful for analyses that combine qualifying position with driver/constructor metadata. | Use for: compare qualifying vs race results; driver qualifying performance by season or circuit; join qualifying session times to driver attributes

accepted.name: race_results_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.result_id,
  r.race_id,
  r.driver_id,
  r.constructor_id,
  r.number,
  r.grid,
  r.position,
  r.position_text,
  r.position_order,
  r.points,
  r.laps,
  r.time,
  r.milliseconds,
  r.fastest_lap,
  r.fastest_lap_time,
  r.fastest_lap_speed,
  r.status_id,
  races.year,
  races.round,
  races.name AS name,
  races.date,
  d.forename,
  d.surname,
  d.code,
  c.name AS name
FROM results r
LEFT JOIN races ON r.race_id = races.race_id
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON r.driver_id = d.driver_id
LEFT JOIN constructors c ON r.constructor_id = c.constructor_id
accepted.description: Denormalized per-result rows combining results, races, drivers and constructors. Use as a starting table for most cross-entity analyses (season leaderboards, per-circuit performance, driver career stats). | Use for: season championship tables, points by driver/constructor; per-circuit performance comparisons; career summaries for drivers or constructors

accepted.name: fastest_lap_per_race_driver
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  lap,
  position,
  time,
  milliseconds
FROM lap_times lt
WHERE milliseconds = (
  SELECT MIN(milliseconds) FROM lap_times lt2
  WHERE lt2.race_id = lt.race_id AND lt2.driver_id = lt.driver_id
)
accepted.description: Deterministic fastest lap per (race_id, driver_id). Useful when lap_times may have multiple records per lap or when selecting best lap per driver in a race. | Use for: identify each driver's best lap in a race; compare best-lap performance across drivers or circuits; join fastest lap to results for correlations

accepted.name: driver_lap_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  race_id,
  driver_id,
  COUNT(1) AS lap_count,
  AVG(milliseconds) AS avg_milliseconds,
  MIN(milliseconds) AS min_milliseconds,
  MAX(milliseconds) AS max_milliseconds
FROM lap_times
GROUP BY race_id, driver_id
accepted.description: Per race-driver aggregated lap statistics (count, avg, min, max milliseconds). Useful for assessing lap consistency and performance per race. | Use for: driver consistency metrics per race; filter drivers by minimum lap counts and performance; compare average lap times across races or seasons

accepted.name: season_constructor_standings
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.year AS year,
  cs.constructor_id,
  SUM(cs.points) AS total_points,
  MAX(cs.wins) AS wins
FROM constructor_standings cs
LEFT JOIN races ON cs.race_id = races.race_id
GROUP BY races.year, cs.constructor_id
accepted.description: Cumulative constructor points per season and constructor. Aggregates constructor_standings (which are snapshots) into season totals — useful as a canonical season-level constructor leaderboard. | Use for: season-level constructor rankings; trend of constructor points across seasons; join to constructors for leaderboards

accepted.name: driver_standings_snapshot
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  races.year AS year,
  ds.driver_id,
  SUM(ds.points) AS total_points,
  MAX(ds.wins) AS wins
FROM driver_standings ds
LEFT JOIN races ON ds.race_id = races.race_id
GROUP BY races.year, ds.driver_id
accepted.description: Season cumulative driver points aggregated from driver_standings snapshots. Useful for driver championship tables and season comparisons. | Use for: season driver leaderboards; career totals by summing across years; compare driver and constructor season performance
